reauth_confirm.title: Sign in to Ohmie again
reauth_confirm.description: Ohmie did not accept the saved sign-in. Sign in again to keep your plans and devices working.

home.title: Your Ohmie home
home.description: Pick the Ohmie home that this Home Assistant belongs to.

new_home.title: Create your Ohmie home
new_home.description: Ohmie keeps one home per person. Next you tell Ohmie about this site and its devices. Ohmie stores no name or address: only the grid node nearest to you.

site_pick.title: Which site is this?
site_pick.description: A home can have more than one site, for example a bach. Each site is set up from its own Home Assistant.

site.title: This site
site.description: Ohmie prices your site at the nearest grid node. It uses your Home Assistant location to find it, then forgets the location.

data_description.icp: Your ICP (on your power bill) lets Ohmie add your lines company's charges and losses, so plans use your total price. It is stored encrypted and never shown again.
data_description.breaker_a: Sets how much power the site can draw at once.
data_description.export_kw: The most your site may send to the grid, from your network's connection approval.

devices.title: Devices
devices.description: Devices already in Ohmie for this site: {existing}. Ohmie found {found} more in Home Assistant. Pick the ones to add.

data.manual: Add a device that is not listed

device_model.title: Which {type} is {device}?
device_model.description: Ohmie fills in typical values. You can change them next.

device.title: {device}
device.description: Connect the entities and check the values. Only the essentials are asked.

data.name: Name in Ohmie (lower case, no spaces)
data.voltage: Supply voltage sensor (optional: shows when the network cuts this circuit)
data.switch: Its real switch (optional: Ohmie only reads it)
data.normal_state: When Ohmie is not in control, the Ohmie switch is

data_description.reserve_pct: Ohmie never plans the battery below this, so it is there for a power cut.
data_description.switch: Without a power sensor, Ohmie counts the device's power from this switch being on. Ohmie never turns it on or off.
data_description.normal_state: Ohmie has its own switch for this device (Ohmie · name). Your automation passes it to the real device. This is what Ohmie's switch shows when you pause Ohmie or Ohmie has no plan.

control.title: Suggest, or drive?
control.description: By default Ohmie only suggests: your devices show the plan and you decide. Pick the devices that Ohmie may control. Ohmie never touches your equipment: it changes only its own entities (an Ohmie switch, a Command, a Next charge window), and your own automation, for example an Ohmie blueprint, passes them on, under your own conditions. You can change this at any time, and the Pause switch stops Ohmie at once.

summary.title: Ready

plan.title: Your power plan
plan.description: What you pay is set by your plan with your retailer, not by the market price. Tell Ohmie what is on your bill (rates as printed, GST included) and Ohmie plans on what you really pay. It also lets Ohmie show what a different plan would save you.

data.controlled: I also have a controlled register (ripple control), for example for hot water

data_description.daily_charge: The fixed daily charge on your bill, GST included.
data_description.since: Today, or the day you changed plan or retailer if you are catching up: Ohmie corrects its records from that day.
data_description.controlled: A cheaper rate for devices the lines company may switch off for some hours a day.

plan_controlled.title: Your controlled register
plan_controlled.description: Which devices are on it, how it is priced, and how many hours a day the network guarantees supply (17 is common).

plan_spot.title: Spot: {flow}
plan_spot.description: On spot you pay the wholesale price at your node, the losses and your lines company's charge (Ohmie works these out from your ICP), plus your retailer's margin: per kWh, as a percentage of the energy price, or both. Leave them empty if you do not know them yet.

data.margin_pct: Margin as a percentage of the energy price

data_description.rate_c: As printed on your bill, GST included.

plan_schedule.title: Time of use: {flow}
plan_schedule.description: Next you enter your plan's windows (peak, shoulder, off-peak...), one at a time, as your retailer defines them; they need not match your lines company's. Every hour outside your windows costs the rate below.

plan_window.title: Window {n} of up to {max}: {flow}
plan_window.description: A window may cross midnight, for example 21:00 to 07:00. If two windows overlap, the first one you entered wins.

change_device.description: Correct the values from the device's own label or app. Ohmie plans with them from the next plan.

balancing.title: Load balancing
balancing.description: Pick what reads each phase at your grid connection (its current in A, or its power in W or kW), its voltage if you have it, and each circuit of this site. Then say how much of each limit Ohmie may use; the rest stays free for things nobody controls. Ohmie acts one step at a time: first a device that can slow down (an EV charger), and only then one that switches off. It gives the power back below the release line, at most 15 points lower. A voltage that sags by the set percent counts like an overload. This is not protection: your breakers, fuse and charger stay that.

data.commit_pct: Ohmie may use up to (% of each limit)
data.release_pct: Ohmie gives the power back below (% of each limit)
data.sag_pct: Act when the voltage sags by (%)

invite_pending.title: Your Ohmie invite is pending
invite_pending.description: Your Ohmie account has no active invite yet. When Ohmie tells you it is active: if Ohmie is already set up here, it connects by itself; if you were setting it up, add Ohmie again.

plan_stale.title: No current Ohmie plan for {asset}
plan_stale.description: Ohmie has not sent a plan for {asset} for an hour. If Ohmie drives it, the device goes back to its own normal mode. Check the device's settings in Ohmie.

entity_unavailable.title: {entity} is unavailable
entity_unavailable.description: Ohmie uses {entity} for {asset}, and it has been unavailable for 15 minutes. Check its integration, or connect a different entity: Settings → Ohmie → Configure → Add devices.

consent_outdated.title: Ohmie's terms changed
consent_outdated.description: Ohmie has new terms ({version}). Ohmie keeps driving your devices under the terms you accepted; to accept the new ones, open Ohmie → Configure → Suggest or drive.

init.title: Was the power to {asset} cut?
init.description: Ohmie planned {asset} on from {start} to {end}, but it drew no power and was not full.{notice} Was its supply cut by the network (ripple control)? Your answer teaches Ohmie how often this happens.

error.cannot_connect: Ohmie could not be reached. Try again later.

abort.not_loaded: The Ohmie entry is not loaded.

report.name: Report to Ohmie
report.description: Tell Ohmie what happened to its command for a device. Use it in your own automations: an override hands the device back to its own mode until the next half hour.

asset.name: Device
asset.description: The device's name in Ohmie, for example battery.

outcome.name: Outcome
outcome.description: applied: done as commanded; overridden: changed by hand; failed: the device refused.
